rationale: While the literature confirms that biallelic loss-of-function variants in NAV3 represent a major etiology of autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #621182; Kakar et al., 2025), the proposed genotype-phenotype dichotomy is directly contradicted by existing clinical reports. Ghaffar et al. (2024) demonstrated that all eleven affected individuals harboring biallelic, de novo, or heterozygous NAV3 variants presented with microcephaly, intellectual disability, and behavioral abnormalities, refuting the claim that heterozygous missense variants spare head circumference. Furthermore, Umair et al. (2025) identified a biallelic homozygous missense variant in a patient presenting with ambiguous speech, demonstrating that ambiguous speech is not exclusive to heterozygous variants and that biallelic variants do not uniformly produce complete speech absence.

evidence.text: Ghaffar et al. identified eleven individuals from seven families harboring biallelic, de novo, and heterozygous NAV3 variants, reporting that all affected individuals presented with microcephaly, intellectual disability, skeletal deformities, ocular anomalies, and behavioral issues.

conflicts: Ghaffar et al. (2024) documented microcephaly in all 11 affected individuals irrespective of variant zygosity (biallelic, de novo, and heterozygous), directly conflicting with the hypothesis that heterozygous missense variants lack microcephaly.

Umair et al. (2025) identified ambiguous speech in a patient with a biallelic homozygous missense variant, conflicting with the hypothesis that biallelic cases exhibit complete absence of speech and that ambiguous speech is restricted to heterozygous missense variants.

new_directions.question_text: Does residual microtubule-stabilizing function measured in cell-based assays quantitatively correlate with head circumference and expressive language milestones across NAV3 missense versus truncating variants?
new_directions.rationale: Ghaffar et al. observed impaired microtubule stabilization in vitro; assessing functional assay severity across all published variants will resolve whether phenotype severity is driven by variant mechanism rather than strict monoallelic versus biallelic inheritance.

new_directions.question_text: Are monoallelic/heterozygous NAV3 variants operating via dominant-negative mechanisms or haploinsufficiency in patients presenting with syndromic microcephaly?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying whether dominant variants act through dominant-negative effects on multimerization/microtubule plus-end tracking would explain why heterozygous patients in Ghaffar et al. manifest full syndromic features including microcephaly.
